module_microarchitecture.name: uart_packet_engine
module_microarchitecture.implementation_style: Single-module RTL implementing MMIO decode, control/status registers, two small 16x8 FIFOs, shared baud tick generation, UART TX/RX bit engines, packet counting, and sticky IRQ logic in one synchronous clk domain.
module_microarchitecture.control_strategy: Use simple address decode on wr_en/rd_en to update CONTROL, BAUD_DIV, PACKET_LEN, and IRQ_CLEAR; TX_DATA writes enqueue into the TX FIFO when not full; RX_DATA reads dequeue from the RX FIFO when not empty. A shared baud tick derived from BAUD_DIV advances both TX and RX timing. CONTROL.ENABLE gates overall operation, RX_ENABLE and TX_ENABLE gate the respective datapaths, LOOPBACK routes completed transmitted bytes into the RX acceptance path, and IRQ_ENABLE gates the final irq output from latched IRQ_STATUS bits.
module_microarchitecture.state_strategy: Maintain explicit state for TX and RX UART engines, FIFO write/read pointers, occupancy counters, shift registers, bit counters, baud divider counter, packet byte counters, live status flags, and latched IRQ bits. Use straightforward enumerated states for idle/start/data/stop sequencing in TX and idle/start/data/stop validation in RX. Preserve FIFO level state independently for TX and RX, and update packet_count on accepted valid receive bytes. Keep reset behavior synchronous and deterministic with all registers, counters, pointers, shifters, and status outputs cleared.
module_microarchitecture.output_strategy: Drive rd_data from the selected readable register or zero for unmapped addresses. Drive uart_tx from the TX state machine idle-high output, with no combinational dependence on uart_rx. Drive irq as a level signal from CONTROL.IRQ_ENABLE ANDed with any set IRQ_STATUS bit. Drive rx_fifo_level and tx_fifo_level directly from FIFO occupancy, and mirror packet_count to the debug count output. STATUS reflects live FIFO and busy/error conditions, while IRQ_STATUS holds latched completion and error events until cleared by IRQ_CLEAR.
ownership_notes: Owns all top-level MMIO-visible control, status, and debug behavior exactly as defined by the register contract.
Owns the full UART protocol implementation for 1 start bit, 8 data bits LSB-first, no parity, and 1 stop bit.
Owns the only state elements needed for the requested scale: FIFO storage/pointers/counts, baud counter, shifters, byte/bit counters, packet counters, status flags, and interrupt latches.
Must preserve the exact top-level module name, port names, and register map without introducing extra interfaces or subordinate modules.

fsm_intent.name: tx_uart_fsm
fsm_intent.description: Simple transmit sequencer that remains in idle until CONTROL.ENABLE and CONTROL.TX_ENABLE are asserted and TX FIFO is non-empty. It then emits a start bit, shifts out 8 data bits LSB-first using the shared baud tick, emits one stop bit, and marks byte completion before returning to idle or immediately starting the next byte if more FIFO data is present.

fsm_intent.name: rx_uart_fsm
fsm_intent.description: Simple receive sequencer that waits for a start-bit qualification on uart_rx, samples the data bits using the shared baud tick, checks the stop bit, and either accepts the reconstructed byte or latches framing_error. Valid received bytes are pushed into the RX FIFO when space is available, or latch rx_overflow on full.

datapath_intent.name: register_and_status_datapath
internal_storage: TX FIFO storage and write/read pointers
RX FIFO storage and write/read pointers
output_mapping: rd_data returns the addressed readable register value or zero for unmapped addresses.
STATUS bit assignments follow the live FIFO empty/full, tx_busy, rx_busy, packet_active, and error conditions.
IRQ_STATUS bits hold rx_done, tx_done, rx_overflow, tx_underflow, framing_error, and packet_done until cleared.
rx_fifo_level and tx_fifo_level expose FIFO occupancy truncated or sized to 6 bits as required by the port width.
packet_count output mirrors the internal debug counter value.

datapath_intent.name: uart_tx_datapath
output_mapping: uart_tx is held high in idle and stop state, low for the start bit, and driven by the current transmit shift bit during data bits.
A completed transmitted byte increments the packet accounting path when packet counting semantics are enabled by the top-level control flow.
tx_fifo_level and STATUS.tx_empty/tx_full reflect FIFO occupancy driven by TX push/pop activity.

datapath_intent.name: uart_rx_datapath
output_mapping: Valid framed bytes are pushed into the RX FIFO when enabled and space is available.
Invalid stop-bit sampling latches framing_error into IRQ_STATUS and sets STATUS.error.
Loopback routes completed transmitted bytes into the same RX acceptance path without creating combinational feedback on uart_tx.

sequencing_notes: RESET clears all configuration, FIFO storage/pointers, counters, shifters, state machines, status flags, interrupt latches, irq, rd_data, and packet_count-related outputs.
MMIO writes are handled synchronously on clk; TX_DATA writes only enqueue when TX FIFO is not full, and RX_DATA reads only dequeue when RX FIFO is not empty.
BAUD_DIV is used to generate a deterministic shared baud tick for both TX and RX timing; a zero divider is treated as minimum-division behavior in a simple synthesizable way.
Packet completion is based on valid byte counts, not framing bits; rx_done and tx_done assert when the relevant byte counter reaches PACKET_LEN.
IRQ_STATUS bits are sticky until cleared by IRQ_CLEAR write-one-to-clear semantics, and irq is a level signal gated by CONTROL.IRQ_ENABLE.
Loopback only redirects completed transmitted bytes into the receive acceptance path after transmit completion semantics, not combinationally from uart_tx.
timing_notes: Single synchronous clock domain only; no additional clock or reset domains are introduced.
The shared baud tick is derived from clk and BAUD_DIV with no requirement for fractional timing.
UART TX and RX state machines advance only on baud-tick events and therefore remain straightforward and synthesizable.

The implementation intent favors small, explicit counters and state registers rather than deep control logic, while still reaching the requested roughly 150-200 flip-flop scale through the two FIFOs, counters, shifters, and status/IRQ state.
consistency_notes: No hierarchy, ports, or filenames may differ from digital_spec_json.
